messages:
megan-support: FYI - AcmeCorp just opened a high-priority ticket. They see intermittent 502 / timeouts from the hosted API for their inference route and are reporting duplicate billing when clients retry. Customer impact: multiple production customers reporting failures.

alex-engineering: Can you paste an example trace ID or request payload? We need to know if upstream success is happening but the gateway is returning an error.

megan-support: Trace IDs from customer: trace=tc-8d3f2a1e, tc-8d3f2a9f, tc-8d3f2b22. Sample curl they used:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' 
  -H 'Idempotency-Key: 1234-5678' 
  -d '{"input":"summarize:..."}' -v
```

samir-sre: Pulling logs now. Early look: gateway shows upstream responded 200 for tc-8d3f2a1e but connection closed while proxy flushing, so gateway returned 502 to client. That would explain duplicate billing if client retries and backend actually processed the original.

nate-runtime: Confirming: runtime logs show model served tokens and emitted final chunk for those traces. We have evidence of downstream success + proxy-level failure.

maria-ops: Any recent deploys to the edge/proxy in the last 30m? I see a canary pushed ~45m ago to the edge pool (rollout id: roll-20270318-7).

alex-engineering: That canary changes keepalive/write-timeout defaults. If the keepalive is too short we'll see proxied connections cut while backend still streams.

samir-sre: Reproducing locally with a short timeout shows the same pattern. Gateway log snippet: 

```
[E] proxy: upstream closed connection (write: broken pipe) trace=tc-8d3f2a1e route=/v1/generate client=ACME-APP
[E] proxy: returning 502 to client after upstream partial write
```

megan-support: Customer wants an ETA and asks if there's a mitigation that avoids duplicate billing.

nate-runtime: Immediate mitigation idea: enable strict idempotency enforcement at the gateway for requests that include Idempotency-Key header, rejecting retries within a short window with 409 instead of forwarding. That prevents duplicate processing while we fix timeouts.

alex-engineering: We can enable a temporary proxy patch (feature-flagged) that checks Idempotency-Key and returns 202/409 based on a fast in-memory store. Implement low-risk TTL 5 minutes. Deployment to edge can be rolled out within ~30 mins with canary.

maria-ops: For customers without idempotency keys, we can increase proxy write-timeout from 5s to 20s as an emergency config to reduce connection cutoff. Rollback timestamp and metrics monitored.

samir-sre: I'll open an incident mitigation runbook: set edge write-timeout to 20s for pools EU/US, flip new idempotency feature flag on canary zone, monitor p95 and 5xx.

megan-support: Communicating to AcmeCorp: ask them to add Idempotency-Key header as short-term workaround and we'll offer credits for any duplicate charges while we remediate.

alex-engineering: Action items: 
- alex-engineering: PR for idempotency-check feature flag + lightweight in-memory key store (PR #4321).
- nate-runtime: add metric instrumentation to emit "upstream-closed-after-success" counter.
- samir-sre: apply edge write-timeout increase and flip canary for idempotency flag, roll forward if green.
- megan-support: send initial customer comms and offer credits; collect any additional trace IDs.
- maria-ops: prepare rollback plan and post-change monitoring dashboard.

incident-bot: Incident created: hosted-502-doublecharge-1779998888. Priority: P1. Assigned: alex-engineering, samir-sre, nate-runtime, megan-support.

megan-support: I'll draft the customer note now and ping legal for credits.

alex-engineering: ETA for PR + canary deploy ~35m. I'll link PR here when ready.

samir-sre: Edge config change applied to canary pool at +00:18. Observing 5xx drop in canary. If green for 10 minutes, we push to remainder.

nate-runtime: Instrumentation landed (internal metric name: upstream_success_but_conn_closed). Hooked to alerts at >1/min rate.

megan-support: Customer updated: applied mitigation for their region, asked to retry with Idempotency-Key. They accepted temporary credit offer.

alex-engineering: Canary looks good. Rolling to remaining edge pools.

samir-sre: Rolling now. Keeping monitoring on high cadence.

maria-ops: Postmortem checklist:
- root cause: edge proxy write-timeout too aggressive following recent canary change.
- short-term mitigation: increased write-timeout + idempotency enforcement.
- long-term actions: add end-to-end integration test for streaming flush with simulated slow clients; persist idempotency keys in a small shardable store (not ephemeral in-memory) and documentation for default client retry behavior.

megan-support: Thanks team. I'll assemble postmortem and include customer comms + credit details. Assigning owners in the doc.

alex-engineering: PR link: https://git.redwood.ai/p/r/redwood/proxy/merge/4321 - contains feature-flagged idempotency + tests.

samir-sre: Closing warroom in 45m if metrics remain stable.

megan-support: Ending notes: credits approved, customer satisfied with mitigation, will follow up with long-term rollout timeline. :white_check_mark:
